one_liner: Sharded concurrent Rust cache with S3-FIFO/CLOCK-Pro-style eviction; beats Mutex-guarded LRU mainly on hit ratio and thread scaling.
what_it_does: quick_cache is a bounded in-memory key-value cache crate that comes in two types. `sync::Cache` is thread-safe: every method takes &self, and you share it through an Arc. `unsync::Cache` is single-threaded and its `get` returns `&Val`. The constructor takes an estimated item count plus a weight capacity, with an optional per-item `Weighter`, hasher and `Lifecycle` hooks. The sync `get` returns a clone of the value, so large values should be wrapped in Arc. On top of get/insert/remove it adds single-flight loading on a miss (`get_or_insert_with`, `get_value_or_guard`, both with async variants), a closure-based `entry` API, non-blocking `try_*` methods, pinning, iter/drain and `set_capacity`; there is no TTL or expiry.
how_it_is_fast: The eviction policy is a modified CLOCK-Pro that the crate docs call very similar to S3-FIFO. Resident entries live in hot and cold FIFO rings (the hot target defaults to 97% of weight) and carry a small reference counter capped at 2 (the source notes CLOCK-Pro uses 1 and S3-FIFO 3). A ghost ring holds hashes of recently evicted keys (sized at 50% of estimated items by default), and a key that returns while still in it is readmitted straight to hot. This scan resistance is where the hit-ratio gains over LRU come from. A hit only does a relaxed atomic increment of that counter under a shard read lock, and skips it when the counter is already saturated, so reads never need exclusive access or list relinking the way LRU does. The sync cache is split into power-of-two shards (default 4x detected cores). Each shard is a hashbrown HashTable of indices into a linked slab, behind a parking_lot RwLock. Per-entry overhead is 21 bytes, and the cache does not allocate once the table stops growing.
when_to_use: Rust services where many threads share one cache on a hot path: in the README's mokabench runs on the ARC S3 trace at 100k capacity, QuickCache took 2.196 s with 1 client, 1.279 s with 3 and 0.798 s with 6.

Traces with scans or one-hit wonders (storage block traces, buffer caches) where LRU hit ratio collapses: on ARC S3 at 100k entries QuickCache hit 12.8% vs 2.3% for LRU+Mutex, and on DS1 at 1M entries 14.9% vs 3.1%.
Caches sized in bytes rather than item count, using a `Weighter` such as value length. Zero-weight items are kept apart from eviction and never evicted.
Loaders that must compute each missing value only once (thundering-herd protection), sync or async, via `get_or_insert_with` / `get_or_insert_async` / `get_value_or_guard_async`.
When you want a small dependency tree and no background threads. The README contrasts it with Moka, which has more features.
when_not_to_use: You need TTL/TTI expiry or time-based invalidation: the README says these are partially or not implemented and points to Moka. Eviction listeners exist only as a `Lifecycle::on_evict` hook that you write yourself.

You need strict LRU order or a guarantee that a just-replaced item stays resident: the maintainer confirms replaced entries can still be evicted (issue #50), and `insert` vs guarded insert could pick different victims before fix #95 (issue #93).

Tiny caches, or item weights that vary widely on high-core machines: capacity is divided per shard, so an item heavier than one shard's hot budget (about 97% of capacity/shards) is rejected outright, and a shard can evict while other shards still have room (issues #26, #55, #65).
Single-threaded speed is the goal: single-client LRU+Mutex finished faster in 3 of the 9 README configurations (S3 800k: 2.613 vs 3.207 s; DS1 1M: 8.901 vs 9.883 s; SPC1 2M: 10.768 vs 14.611 s).

Processes that must hand memory back after shrinking: evicting or draining drops the items but does not shrink the internal tables (issue #99), and the documented footprint (K+V+21)*(len*1.5).next_power_of_two() includes ghost slots.

integration.dependencies: equivalent 1.0 and hashbrown 0.17 always. Default features add foldhash 0.2 (default hasher) and parking_lot 0.12. Optional: crossbeam-utils 0.8 (`sharded-lock`) and shuttle 0.8 (testing only).
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.85 for 0.7.0 (rust-version in Cargo.toml, checked by cargo-msrv in CI). 0.6.x declared 1.71 but in practice needed 1.80 until fix #121 (issue #118).
integration.platforms: Any Rust std target with no architecture-specific code. CI builds and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows. wasm32 is not documented; an older version failed on wasm32-unknown-unknown through ahash/getrandom (issue #32).
integration.thread_safety: `sync::Cache` is meant to be shared across threads through Arc, with an RwLock per shard (parking_lot by default; crossbeam ShardedLock or std RwLock via features). Gets take a read lock and writes take a write lock. `unsync::Cache` is not thread-safe.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces the Mutex<LruCache> pattern with no external lock, but the constructor (estimated items plus weight capacity), clone-on-get semantics and approximate S3-FIFO-style eviction order all differ from a strict LRU, so call sites and any ordering assumptions have to change.

gotchas: The shard count defaults to 4x detected cores, so `capacity()` is rounded and can differ between machines. Keep `estimated_items_capacity` within about 1-2 orders of magnitude of reality, or set `shards()` explicitly (the maintainer suggests 0 estimated items in tests to force 1 shard).

`Weighter::weight` must be cheap and stable: changing a resident item's weight is documented as undefined behavior (except inside `before_evict`), and so is overflowing the weight sum in release builds.

`Lifecycle` hooks such as `on_evict` and `is_pinned` run inside the eviction path under the shard write lock, so keep them tiny (the eviction-listener example sends to a channel). 0.7.0 broke the Lifecycle API: `RequestState` must now implement Default and is passed by &mut.

The README says it uses 'only trivially verifiable' unsafe, but the source has about 47 unsafe sites (unreachable_unchecked, unchecked slab access, raw pointers in the placeholder waiters). CI runs Miri, cargo-fuzz and shuttle. Recent fixes include a JoinFuture race (#104), a leak when a guard was dropped without inserting (#120) and weight_capacity=1 storing nothing (#106).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you are in Rust and want an in-process S3-FIFO-style cache library. The closest siblings are Caffeine (JVM, W-TinyLFU with expiry and listeners) and otter or golang-fifo (Go); the S3-FIFO and SIEVE entries are libCacheSim research prototypes, not embeddable Rust crates.
verified_claims_summary: The author ran mokabench (the Moka project's ARC-trace replay harness; both caches used an xxh3 hasher) on x64 Linux with an i9-12900H; rustc version and flags are not stated. On the ARC S3 trace at 100k capacity, QuickCache hit 12.84% in 2.196 s with one client, vs 2.33% in 2.422 s for hashlink LruCache behind a Mutex: about 1.1x faster and 5.5x the hit ratio. Across all traces the hit-ratio gain was 1.2-5.5x (equal at SPC1 30M), but LRU+Mutex was only ever run with one client and was faster in 3 of 9 configurations. Also, the README says LRU+Mutex used std::sync::Mutex, but mokabench's hashlink driver actually uses parking_lot::Mutex.
status_note: Actively maintained: v0.7.0 shipped 2026-06-27, it is MIT-licensed, and crates.io shows about 27.2M downloads and 115 reverse dependencies. It is still pre-1.0, and minor releases have broken the API (0.7.0 Lifecycle reshape).
